    A practical assessment reference on mathematics for engineers and researchers

    Words: 2175

    A map of mathematics on three levels of maturity: nine areas, six pages of practice, and one question asked of every fact.

    The main idea of this page #

    Mathematics is taught in pieces and in order of the pupil's age: arithmetic first, then algebra, then geometry, then analysis. Ten years after school what remains is a set of tricks without a map. A person remembers that a derivative is a speed, but not where it comes from, why it needed the completeness of the number line, or at which point the familiar rule stops working. This site is built the other way round. It follows dependencies rather than age: each area rests on the previous one and does not repeat it. Nine areas, and not one of them hangs in the air.

    And every fact here is asked three different questions rather than written out in three different lengths. A school leaver wants to know why it is true, on numbers and on a picture. A student has to compute it and prove it. A professor cares where the statement breaks and why. One and the same fact survives all three questions, and that is the only honest test of whether you understand it.

    The map: nine areas and six pages of practice #

    The fifteen pages of the course fall into three unequal parts. The first nine are the subject itself: an area, its language and its limits. The next three are worked examples by level, where the computation is carried through to a number. The last three are question banks, fifty per level, each answer explained. Plus the glossary and the navigator, which cut across the course.

    The order of the nine areas is neither arbitrary nor the order of a textbook. It is the order in which no area can be read before the one it stands on:

    • 01 · Language and logic. Statement, set, mapping, quantifier, induction and the word «proof» itself. This is the entrance: the vocabulary the other eight speak. It also teaches the writing system and how its signs are pronounced.
    • 02 · Number. From natural to integer, rational, real and complex. Every extension appeared because the previous one could not solve an equation already written down, and every one of them brought something: order, density, completeness, closure.
    • 03 · The discrete. Counting, permutations, recurrences, graphs. Everything finite lives here; here the first group appears, as permutations, and the first limit, as a recurrence.
    • 04 · Algebra. Group, ring, field, vector space. The area about rules of operation mattering more than the nature of the objects, and about why an equation of the fifth degree has no formula in radicals.
    • 05 · Linear algebra. Matrices, forms, eigenvalues. The only case solved completely by an algorithm, with a machine answer to every question. Geometry comes from here too: the scalar product, length, angle.
    • 06 · Analysis. Limit and continuity on the line, derivative, integral, series. The area where the completeness of topic 02 and the rigour of topic 01 are needed for the first time: here «for every, there exists» stops being a formality.
    • 07 · Many variables. Gradient, Jacobian, multiple integral, differential equations. The derivative stops being a number and becomes a linear map, that is, topic 05, and the equations turn out to be the way a law of nature is written.
    • 08 · Randomness. Measure, distribution, the law of large numbers, statistical inference. It stands on the counting of topic 03 and the integral of topic 06, and answers the question nobody else asks: what are we entitled to claim having seen a finite sample.
    • 09 · The boundaries. Topology as continuity without distance, computability and its price, the incompleteness theorems. The area about where the method fails: what cannot be computed, what cannot be proved inside a system, and what stays true when the coordinates are taken away.

    Then come six pages of practice and two transversal tools:

    • 10 · Examples at school level. Nine worked cases where intuition is checked against the count: percentages, scale, average speed, birthdays, order of magnitude, accumulated rounding.
    • 11 · Examples at student level. Seven worked cases where the answer has a quality: Newton's convergence, the remainder of a series, conditioning, quadrature formulas, least squares, the square root law of Monte Carlo.
    • 12 · Examples at professor level. Seven cases where a correct formula gives a wrong answer: a rearranged conditionally convergent series, the loss of associativity, two limits that refuse to swap, Simpson's paradox, a discovery out of nothing, lost significant digits, sensitivity to initial data.
    • 13, 14, 15 · Questions at the same three levels, fifty per page, each with a full answer and the line that says why the question gets asked.
    • The glossary keeps the definitions and the signs of mathematical writing in one place, and the navigator looks at the whole subject through nine engineering lenses: what it is made of, where it is strong, where it breaks, how the areas feed each other, and what a computation costs.

    What is not on this map and why. You will not find geometry and trigonometry as separate pages, and that is a decision rather than an omission. On a map of the subject they are not areas but instruments: geometry lives inside linear algebra, where the scalar product gives it, and trigonometry inside analysis, where sine and cosine appear as series and as solutions of the simplest differential equation. Numerical methods, mathematics for machine learning, game theory and applied statistics did not fit into nine areas at all, which is the sign that each holds a course of its own rather than a tenth section of this one. The last two are named in the seventh section of the chapter on randomness: they stand on the same foundation and begin exactly where that chapter ends.

    Three levels, and why they are kept apart #

    The levels are named as on the sibling sites of the series, and read mathematically here:

    • Noob - a school leaver. Understands the idea on numbers and on a picture, computes by hand, is not afraid of a symbol seen for the first time. The goal of the level is to take the magic out of mathematics: a formula does not fall from the sky, it can be checked on three examples.
    • Pro - a university student. Owns the technique: computes, proves, knows the conditions under which a theorem applies and can name the one being used. The goal is the accuracy that lets a solution be shown to somebody else without falling apart.
    • IGL - a professor. The letters stand for In-Game Leader, and this is the level of the one who holds the whole field: sees where the statement breaks, which assumption was doing the work, what survives a weakening of the premises and which counterexample closes the question. The goal is to understand not only what is true, but why it stops being true.

    One fact on three levels #

    Take an equality that has been argued about on the internet for twenty years: the infinite decimal 0.999... equals one. Watch how the conversation changes with the level.

    Noob. One third is written as 0.333... Multiply both sides by three: the left gives one, the right gives 0.999... So it is the same number written two ways. A notation and a number are different things, and one number can have two notations.

    Pro. By definition 0.999... means the sum of an infinite series of nines over powers of ten. That is a geometric progression with ratio one tenth, its partial sums equal one minus one tenth to the power n, and the limit of that sequence is one. The proof reduces to the definition of a limit: for any positive number there is an index beyond which the difference is smaller. There is no «infinitely small remainder» at the end of the notation, because the notation has no end.

    IGL. The equality holds not by itself but in the field of real numbers with the standard metric and the standard definition of a limit. It rests on completeness and on the Archimedean property: together they forbid a positive number smaller than every fraction one tenth to the power n. Remove the Archimedean property, pass to the hyperreals, and the difference stops being zero while staying infinitesimal. The question at this level is: which property of the number line were you using when you said «obviously»?

    The three levels are not three lengths of text but three different questions about one fact: how to convince yourself, how to prove it, and where it stops working.

    How to use this #

    There are three ways through the site, and the one to choose depends on why you came.

    • You want the map. Read the areas in order from the first: the order is built so that no page needs knowledge from a later one. This is the longest path and the only one that leaves the subject visible whole.
    • You are preparing for an interview or an exam. Start with the question bank at your level and move into an area when an answer turns out to be unclear. Every answer points at the area and the glossary article where its ground lies.
    • You came for one thing. The search looks through every page at once and shows which section holds the hit, and the glossary explains a term away from the page where it first appeared.

    What is deliberately absent: exercises with answer checking and accumulated scores. That would turn a reference into a trainer, and a trainer needs entirely different things.

    What this site can do #

    • Works without a network and without installation. Ordinary pages that open straight from a file, print on paper and are read aloud by a speech synthesizer.
    • Search across every page runs in the browser without a server: the index is built in advance and sits next to the pages.
    • Three font sizes and two themes. The buttons in the top right corner remember your choice between visits, and formulas change size together with the text.
    • Formulas are text, not pictures. They are printed as mathematical markup when the page is built: read aloud, scaled with the text, selectable and printable.
    • The glossary opens inside the reading. Concepts are marked up in the text as cards, and the signs of the writing system are collected in a reference of their own, with pronunciations.
    • Diagrams are drawn in the page itself. Eleven of them, all in the single colour of the theme, so they neither glare at night nor need a second copy.
    • Every computation has been run. If a number is printed on a page, the site's manifest holds the command that produces it, and that command runs at every check. No command in the manifest means no claim on the page.

    What the site holds today #

    The course is written in full. Nine areas of the map, three pages of examples and three banks of fifty questions: fifteen pages of continuous text rather than a table of contents. Across them lie two tools: the navigator with its nine engineering lenses and the glossary, where fifty four concepts and eighty five signs of mathematical writing are kept together with their pronunciations.

    What that means in practice. Formulas are printed as real mathematical markup: a speech synthesizer pronounces them, the font buttons enlarge them, they can be selected with the mouse and they survive printing, and all of it without a single line of code running in your browser. Concepts are marked up inside the text: meeting an unfamiliar word, you open a card without losing your place. Eleven diagrams are drawn where a picture explains faster than three paragraphs: the definition of a limit, a secant turning into a tangent, columns under a curve, the bell from a sum of dice.

    And the promise that is checked by a machine rather than by a word: every computation shown is run at every check, and every printed number has a command in the manifest that produces it. Fifty four blocks of computation and thirty three claims are verified again whenever a page changes. That is how several numbers written from memory turned out to be wrong: it was not an eye that caught them but a run.

    What is not here yet: the English, Ukrainian and German versions of the chapters. This landing page is translated; the rest wait their turn and say so honestly, with a card linking to the Russian text.

    What you have after this page #

    • A map of the subject in nine areas, with the reason they come in this order and which one rests on which.
    • Three levels of maturity, separated not by length but by the question each one asks of the same fact.
    • A sample of such a treatment on the equality 0.999... = 1, showing what a school leaver, a student and a professor each answer.
    • An understanding of what counts as proved here: a number on a page lives together with the command that produces it.
